e_en: Tsunami is caused by underwater volcanic activity. A sudden movement of the ocean because of earthquakes or landslides on the sea floor causes tsunami waves. They can also be initiated because of volcanic eruptions beneath the sea, but that is a rare phenomenon.

q_en: Which economist gave the theory of Opportunity Cost?
e_en: Gottfried Haberler gave the theory of Opportunity Cost. Opportunity cost is the value of the most valuable choice from those which were not taken. It expresses the basic relation between choice and scarcity. Gottfried Haberler abandoned the labor theory of value for this concept.

India has a land boundary of about 15,200 km whereas the total length of the coastline of the mainland, including Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep, is 7,516.6 km, of this the mainland coastline length is 5422.6 kilometers whereas Island territories coastline length is 2094 kilometers.

q_en: A substantial increase in capital expenditure or revenue deficit leads to ________.
e_en: The correct answer is Option C i.e. Fiscal Deficit. Fiscal Deficit is the sum of revenue and capital expenditure minus(-) all revenue and capital received other than the loan is taken.

q_en: Who was the last ruler of the Vaghela Dynasty of Gujarat after whose defeat the kingdom was passed to Alauddin Khilji?
e_en: The Vaghela dynasty was an Indian dynasty that ruled Gujarat for a short time period in the13th century CE. The Vaghela's were the last Hindu kings to rule large parts of Gujarat, with capital Dholka before the Alauddin Khilji's army conquest of the region. In 1304, a second attack by Alauddin's forces defeated Karandev, the last ruler of the Vaghela Dynasty of Gujarat and permanently ended the Vaghela dynasty.

q_en: To which of the following Indian states does the tribe of 'Nyishi' belong?
e_en: Nyishi is one of the major ethnic groups and major tribes in the northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh. It is also known by the name Bangni and Dafla in some areas of Arunachal Pradesh. The people belonging to the Nyishi tribe are also found in eastern Bhutan and they speak Tibeto-Burman language of the Sino-Tibetan family. They support themselves with slash-and-burn agriculture and with hunting and fishing.

q_en: What effect will a decrease in demand and an increase in supply have on equilibrium price?
o_en: Sometimes price will rise and sometimes it will fall
e_en: The correct answer is option A, i.e. Equilibrium price will fall. </span

q_en: Which of the following Indian film-makers was given the title of 'Ambassador of Interlaken' in 2011 at Switzerland?
e_en: The famous Indian filmmaker Yash Chopra was given the honorary title of 'Ambassador of Interlaken' in 2011 in Switzerland. Interlaken is a small town in mountainous Bernese Oberland region of central Switzerland. A 250 kg bronze statue was made in the year 2016 in Kursaal garden in Interlaken, Switzerland by the government of Switzerland for his work in the cinema industry and boosting the popularity of alpine nation among Indian tourist.

q_en: Who is the author of the book 'India Shastra: Reflections on the Nation in our Time'?
e_en: 'India Shastra: Reflections on the Nation in our Time' book is written by well known Indian politician, writer, and a former career international diplomat. The government of India changed in 2014 and BJP came to power after winning the 16th Lok Sabha elections. This book was published in the year 2015 and it is basically about the transformation of India’s politics, economy, foreign policy, media, civil rights, governance, etc.

q_en: Dashain is the grandest festival of _________.
e_en: Dashain is the biggest festival of Nepal which is also celebrated in several parts of India. It is mainly celebrated for two weeks with prayers and offerings to Durga, the Universal Mother Goddess. The famous festival Fulpatti is also celebrated during these days. It is observed on the 7th day of the Dashain festival. Extra Information : Nepal is a landlocked country whose capital is Kathmandu and currency is Nepalese rupee (NPR).

q_en: Which Indian batsman was the first to hit six consecutive sixes in first-class cricket?
e_en: Ravi Shastri was the first Indian batsman to hit six consecutive sixes in first-class cricket. He scored six sixes in an over against left-arm spinner Tilak Raj in the year 1985 in a Ranji Trophy match between Bombay and Baroda. Ravi Shastri also scored the fastest ever double century in first-class cricket history in the same match.

q_en: In the year ________, the Maratha Empire ceased to exist with the surrender of the Marathas to the British, ending the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
e_en: The Third Anglo-Maratha War ended in 1818 with the surrender of the Marathas to the British. The Third Anglo-Maratha War took place in Maharashtra and its neighboring areas in 1817 and 1818. The main reason for the Third Anglo-Maratha war was British conflict with the Pindaris whom the British suspected were being protected by the Marathas. The Treaty of Mandasor was signed between the British and the Holkar chief in 1818.

q_en: __________ has been established as the annual 'International Day of Happiness'.

e_en: Correct answer: China.

q_en: During World War II, the Battles of Kohima and Imphal were fought in the year ________.
e_en: The Battles of Kohima and Imphal were fought between 8 March and 18 July 1944. In 1944, during the rise of the Second World War, the Japanese forces attacked the northeast region of India through Burma. They attacked Imphal first and then they move towards Kohima the capital city of Nagaland. The British and Indian forces fought valiantly and prevented the ambitious plans of Japan, resulting in the fiercest battles of Kohima and Imphal.

q_en: The term 'Dolphin Kick' is associated with which sport?
e_en: The Dolphin kick is associated with the Swimming. The Dolphin kick technique is used by professional swimmers, they use that motion that propels them forward underwater after diving in, and at the underwater turns.

q_en: Which of the following is the highest mountain peak in Maharashtra?
e_en: Kalsubai Shikhar is the highest mountain peak in Maharashtra. It is also called Everest of Maharashtra having an elevation of 5400 feet (1636 m). The mountain range and peak lies inside the Kalsubai Harishchandragad sanctuary, situated at an elevation of 5400 feet. Salher is the second highest

q_en: Which article for the Constitution of India provides that each Indian state will have a governor?
e_en: Article 153 in the Constitution of India provides that there shall be a Governor for each State. The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 facilitated the appointment of the same person as governor for two or more states.

q_en: Which player has the record of scoring the most runs in the history of ICC World Cup?
e_en: Sachin Tendulkar, from 1992-2011 has hit a total of 2278 runs in World cup matches, with the highest number of centuries(6) and the highest number of 4's(241). He is followed by Ricky Pointing with 1743 runs. World Cup Trivia Details Highest team score 417–6 made by Australia against Afghanistan in 2015. Lowest team score 36 runs made by Canada against Sri Lanka in 2003. Highest match aggregate 688–18 was between Australia vs Sri Lanka in 2015.

q_en: The easternmost point of India is _____.
e_en: The correct answer is Kibithu. The Eastern most village of India is Kibithu , nested in the Mishmi hills of Arunachal Pradesh . It is located in the juncture of India, China and Myanmar. It is located on the last road head of the extreme northeast of northeastern India. The Lohit River enters India at Kibithu.

q_en: In Parliament, who takes the final decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not?
e_en: Lok Sabha Speaker certifies the bill as a money bill before sending it to the upper house, and the decision of the Speaker is binding on both the Houses.He/she represents the full authority of the House and decides whether a bill is a money bill or not. A money bill or supply bill is a bill that solely concerns taxation or government spending. The Speaker appoints the Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha. The Lok Sabha speaker is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha.

q_en: What is the other name for 'Orion' Constellation?
e_en: Orion constellation is one of the brightest and best known constellations in the night sky. It lies on the celestial equator. Orion has been known since ancient times. The constellation is also known as the Hunter, as it is associated with one in Greek mythology. It represents the mythical hunter Orion, who is often depicted in star maps as either facing the charge of Taurus, the bull.

q_en: Which of the following is called the 'Grand Canyon of India'?
e_en: The Gorge of Gandikota is situated on the Pennar River in Andhra Pradesh . It is known as the Grand Canyon of India. The Grand Canyon is located in Arizona, USA. A gorge is a valley formed by a source of water flowing between tall slabs of steep rocks.The Pennar river must have cut rocks in Gandokota over centuries to have formed the Canyon which we see today.

q_en: What is the economic impact of increase in productivity of firms?
o_en: The impact may vary among nations and their economic conditions
No change in Gross Domestic Product
e_en: If Firms located in India Increase productivity , more business is done by them, leading to greater profits and enhanced economic activity. Gross domestic product is the measure of a country’s domestic economic activities. It is the sum of prices or market values of all the final goods and services which are produced in an economy during a specific period of time.

q_en: The Aligarh Movement was started by ______.
e_en: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan is associated with the Aligarh Movement. He organised and founded the Aligarh Movement​ in 1875. It was based in Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh. Major objectives of the Aligarh Movement: To provide modern education among Indian Muslims without weakening their allegiance to Islam. To initiate social reforms among Muslims relating to purdah, polygamy, widow remarriage, women’s education, slavery, divorce, etc.

q_en: Which one of the following is the largest recognised constellation?
e_en: Hydra is the largest constellation. It measures 1303 square degrees and it is also the longest at over 100 degrees. Centaurus is the brightest constellation. Crux, also known as the Southern Cross is the smallest constellation. Canis Major constellation contains the brightest star Sirius. Constellation is a group of stars that form a particular pattern and are generally named according to the shape it has. There are officially 88 constellations recognized so far.

q_en: Rehuke khim' or 'cowrie shawl' are traditional textiles of ______.
e_en: Rehuke khim or cowrie shawl is the most important cloth meant for the rich man of the Yimchunger tribe in Nagaland. In Naga society, cowrie is a symbol of marital status. One of the most common cloth used by both men and women without any restriction is a black shawl called Aneadk Khim.

q_en: Who is the author of the book 'The Bird of Time: Songs of Life, Death and the Spring'?
e_en: The author of the book 'The Bird of Time: Songs of Life, Death and the Spring' is Sarojini Naidu. She was the first female to become the governor of an Indian state. She became governor of Uttar Pradesh. She is also known as 'Nightingale of India'. She also wrote poetry, her works include Golden Threshold, The Bird of Time, The Sceptred Flute and The Feather of the Dawn.

q_en: Identify the element that is most prolific in the crust of the earth.
e_en: Oxygen is the most abundant element found in the earth crust. Oxygen accounts to 46.6% of the Earth Crust. O > Si > Al > Fe > Ca are the most abundant element in earth crust. Aluminium is the most abundant metal in the earth's crust.

On May 7 his birth anniversary was celebrated all over India. Songs written by are used as the national anthem for India and Bangladesh.

Time in the first half of the parliamentary proceeding

Prabhu Desai. The headquarter of SAG at Panaji, Goa. Pramod Sawant is the current Chief Minister of Goa.

q_en: Todar Mal was _______ at Emperor Akbar's court.
e_en: Raja Todar Mal was the Finance Minister of the Mughal empire during Akbar's reign. Raja Todar Mal:- He was one of the Navaratna's in Akbar's 'darbar' Raja Todar Mal introduced standard weights and measures, a land survey and settlement system, revenue districts and officers. He introduced a new system of revenue known as zabt and a system of taxation called dahshala. The Kashi Vishwanath Temple was rebuilt in 1585 by Todar Mal.

q_en: _____ rulers established their religious capital in Khajuraho.
e_en: Chandela rulers established their religious capital in Khajuraho. Chandela:- The Chandelas of Jejakabhukti was a royal dynasty in Central India. Nannuka was the founder of Chandela dynasty of India. They ruled much of the Bundelkhand region (then called Jejakabhukti) between the 9th and the 13th centuries. The Chandelas are well known for their art and architecture, most notably for the temples at their original capital Khajuraho.

q_en: _____ made Agra the capital of his empire.

q_en: B R Ambedkar was independent India's first _____ minister.
e_en: Dr B R Ambedkar was independent India's first law minister. He is popularly known as Babasaheb Ambedkar. He was independent India's first law and justice minister, the architect of the Constitution of India, and a founding father of the Republic of India. He campaigned against social discrimination towards the untouchables (Dalits). In 1990, the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, was posthumously conferred upon B R Ambedkar.

q_en: ________ was the ﬁrst sportsperson to receive the Padma Vibhushan award.
e_en: Viswanathan Anand was the ﬁrst sportsperson to receive the Padma Vibhushan award. He is an Indian chess grandmaster and a former World Chess Champion. He occupied the number one position for 21 months, the 6th longest on record. Anand was also the first recipient of the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award in 1991–92, India's highest sporting honour. He is also regarded as one of the greatest rapid players of all time.

q_en: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
e_en: The correct answer is Koshi. Koshi river originates from Nepal. It is known as Saptakoshi, as it is joined by seven upper tributaries. It is almost 470 km long from the Himalayan point till it merges to the Ganga river in Bihar.

q_en: Khichdi, Uttarayan and Lohri are different names of the festival _________.
e_en: The correct answer is option A) i.e. Makar Sankranti. Makar Sankranti is celebrated in various parts of India to observe the day which marks the shift of the sun into ever-lengthening days. It also marks the beginning of the end of Winter and the harvest of rabi crops. While Makar Sankranti is most popular in West India, down south, the festival is known as Pongal and in the north, it is celebrated as Lohri.

q_en: The 'Treaty of Mangalore' was signed between the British East India Company and ________.

q_en: _________ of India won an Academy Award for the costume design in 1982.
e_en: Oscar Awards, officially known as Academy Awards, was won by the Bhanu Athaiya in the category of best costume design in 1982. She has also won two National Awards in 1992 and 2002.

q_en: Which of the following Indian cities is known as the 'zero mile city' because of its location?
e_en: Nagpur is also known as '; Zero Mile Center' of India. It is because of the Nagpur is the geographical centre point of India and all the distances of major cities marked on pillars are measured starting this point.

q_en: Which of the following is mined in the Badampahar mines of Odisha?
e_en: The iron ore, Hematite mined in the Badampahar mines of Odisha. In Odisha-Jharkhand belt, the high-grade hematite ore is found in Badampahar mines in the Mayurbhanj and Kendujhar districts. In the adjoining Singbhum district of Jharkhand, hematite iron ore is mined in Gua and Noamundi. Very high-grade hematites are also found in the famous Bailadila range of hills in the Bastar district of Chhattisgarh.

e_en: The Indian National Association was established in 1876 by Surendranath Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose in Calcutta now Kolkata. Surendranath Banerjee, an eminent leader of INC, is also known as RashtraGuru.

e_en: The lone gold medal for India was won by Kavinder Singh Bisht at the 38th GeeBee Boxing Tournament held at Helsinki, Finland. He defeated his opponent Mohammed Hussamuddin in summit clash in the 56kg category. Mohammed Hussamuddin is also an India boxer and he won bronze medal in the same event.

Rani Durgavati preferred to die respectfully while fighting opponents rather than being an imperial slave of Mughals.

The objective of this sport is to create highly energetic atmosphere with continuous leg-kicking on one-hand and constant attempts to hit the target on the other.

q_en: The Tata Iron and Steel company (TISCO) was established by Dorabji Tata in:
e_en: The Tata Iron and Steel company (TISCO) was established by Dorabji Tata in 1907. q_en: A sustained rise in the general price level in an economy is called ________.

q_en: The ________ was a group of seven Members of Parliament from the United Kingdom, constituted to suggest constitutional reforms for British India.
e_en: The Simon Commission(1927) was a group of seven Members of Parliament from the United Kingdom, constituted to suggest constitutional reforms for British India. Sir John Simon was its chairman. A protest against it was led by nationalist Lala Lajpat Rai in Lahore, during which he died because of his injuries in 1928. The Sargent scheme was a 1944 memorandum prepared by the British-run Government of India. It outlined the future development of literacy and education in India.

q_en: Who amongst the following succeeded the Mughal throne in the year 1556?
e_en: Akbar succeeded the Mughal throne in the year 1556 after Humayun. He was the third ruler of the Mughal Emperor. He reigned from 1556 to 1605. Jahangir succeeded him in the year 1605 to become the 4th Mughal Emperor.

q_en: ________ is the oldest golf course outside the United Kingdom.
e_en: Royal Calcutta Golf Club, Kolkata is the oldest golf course outside the United Kingdom. It was established in the year 1829. It is also the second-oldest club outside Scotland. The Royal Blackheath in London is the oldest one outside Scotland, which was established in the year 1776.

q_en: The National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises meets once every ________ months in a year.
e_en: The National Board for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises meets once every 6 months in a year. It was established on 15 May 2007, having 47 members. It is responsible for examining the factors affecting the development and promotion of MSMEs. It also gives advice to the Central government about the use of funds constituted in Section 12.

q_en: The Banking Regulation Act was passed in India in ________.
e_en: The Banking Regulation Act was passed in India in the year 1949. The act regulates all the banking firms in India. It came into effect on 16 March 1949 and was applicable in Jammu and Kashmir from 1956.

q_en: Which of the following is NOT a vocal form of Hindustani classical music?
e_en: Pakhawaj is not a vocal form of Hindustani classical music. It is a two-headed drum which is barrel-shaped, also known as mridang. Tarana, Drupad, Khyal, and Dhamar are major vocal forms of Hindustani classical music. Hindustani classical music originated in 12th century CE. The music has 7 basic notes and 5 interspersed half-notes, which result in a 12-note scale.

q_en: Article ________ of the Constitution of India gives the Election Commission the power to supervise elections to the Parliament and state legislatures.
e_en: Article 324 of the Indian Constitution gives the Election Commission the power to supervise elections to the Parliament and state legislatures. Article 342 deals with Scheduled Tribes in India. Article 314 has been repealed. Article 341 deals with Scheduled Castes of India.

q_en: ________ is the largest river island in the world.
e_en: Majuli is the largest river island in the world. It is situated in Assam on the Brahmaputra river. It is spread across an area of 880 sq km and is inhabited by tribes such as Deori and Mising. The Guinness World Records has declared the Majuli island as the largest river island in the world, toppling Marajo in Brazil to clinch the record.

q_en: Minimum Support Price (MSP) is recommended by ________.

The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
The Commission for Weights and Measures
e_en: The correct answer is Option C i.e. Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP). Minimum Support Price (MSP) is recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP). MSP is a price set by the Indian government at which it purchases crops directly from the farmer. It is an important part of the agricultural policy of India.

q_en: ________ was the first and only Muslim woman to ever sit on the throne of Delhi.
e_en: Razia Sultan was the first and the only Muslim woman to ever sit on the throne of Delhi. She was appointed by Iltutmish. She served as the Sultan of Delhi from 10 October 1236- 14 October 1240. q_en: Which Indian monument was built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh in the year 1799?

q_en: Who had built Taj Mahal, for his wife Mumtaz Mahal along the banks of the Yamuna River in Agra?
e_en: Shah Jahan built Taj Mahal as a memorial for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. It acts as the tomb of Shah Jahan's deceased wife Mumtaz Mahal. The original name of Mumtaz Mahal is Arjumand Banu Begum. The mausoleum was commissioned in 1632 and opened for visitors in 1648. It is now listed in the 7 Wonders Of The World and attracts millions of tourists every year.

q_en: Who won the Nobel Prize in 1906 for his neuron doctrine?
e_en: It was Santiago Ramón y Cajal who won a Nobel Prize along with Camillo Golgi. The prize was won for his neuron doctrine which is a theory that states that the nervous system is made up of discrete nervous cells. He discovered this using a silver staining technique developed by the Italian scientist Camillo Golgi. He first discovered this while investigating cells of bird brains in 1888.

q_en: Which of the following was the most important characteristic of India's trade throughout the colonial period?
e_en: A major trade characteristic of trade in the colonial period of India was its export surplus. An export surplus is when a country exports more products than it imports from other countries. This was because in the colonial period the British allowed large exports of handicraft products and free export of India's raw material. Thus exported goods from India were sought after which led to a high volume of export.

q_en: The Red Fort and the Jama Masjid in Delhi stand out as towering achievements of architecture during the reign of________.
e_en: The Red Fort and Jama Masjid are two of the many architectural gems built in Shah Jahan's reign. Even though Shah Jahan is famously known for the Taj Mahal, the Red Fort and Jama Masjid are the other wonders he built in Delhi itself. The Red Fort was built in 1639 as his palace for his then capital back then known as Shahjahanad. The Jama Masjid was finished in 1656 with a name of Masjid-e-Jahan Numa.

q_en: The Victoria Memorial, conceived by Lord Curzon, represents the architectural climax of _________ city.
e_en: The Victoria Memorial as conceived by Lord Curzon is located in Kolkata. It is a marble architectural wonder present in the city of Kolkata. It was built in memory of Queen Victoria of England after her death in 1901. The building was built between 1906 and 1921 and has now been turned into a museum that attracts thousands of visitors annually.

q_en: Which river passes through maximum number of countries?
e_en: The Danube river in Europe is the river that passes through the maximum number of countries in its journey. It passes through 10 countries: Germany, Hungary, Romania, Austria, Serbia, Bulgaria, Croatia, Moldova, Ukraine, Slovakia. It starts in Southern Germany and runs into the Black Sea through Romania. It is the second-longest river in Europe after the Volga with a length of 2,850 kilometres.

q_en: ___________ won a silver medal at the 38th GeeBee Boxing Tournament which was held at Helsinki, Finland.

q_en: Daringbadi hill station is located in the Indian state of ______.
e_en: Daringbadi hill station is located in the Indian state of Odisha. Daringbadi Hill is Kandhamal district of Odisha state in eastern India. It is situated at a height of 3000 ft. The temperature level of Daringbadi has often been recorded below 0 °C. It is also famous for ginger harvesting.

e_en: The Patharughat Peasant Uprising against the tax policies of the British in 1894. Patharughat is a place in Assam and currently known as Patharighat. It is one of the revenue circles in Darrang District. <s

q_en: The 'Diphu Pass' which is the tri-junction between India, Myanmar and China is on this Border Line?
e_en: Diphu Pass is in Arunachal Pradesh. It is located around the area of the disputed tri-point borders of India, Myanmar, and China and is a mountain pass. Diphu Pass is also a strategic approach to eastern Assam. It lies on the McMahon Line.

q_en: In which year was the term 'Gross Happiness Index' coined by the fourth king of Bhutan, Jigme Singye Wangchuck?
e_en: The term "Gross Happiness Index" was coined by Jigme Singye Wangchuk in 1972. This index is still used by the government of Bhutan to measure the collective happiness and the well-being of a population of Bhutan. The first Prime Minister of Bhutan was Jigme Palden Doorji.

q_en: The Khilafat Movement of 1920 was organised as a protest against the injustice done to _______.
e_en: Khilafat Movement was organised as a protest against the injustice done to Turkey. It was organised by the Indian Muslims in 1919 to recover the Caliph of Turkey as a symbol of unity among Muslim community in India. The movement was also supported by Mahatma Gandhi's Non-Cooperation movement. It was launched by brothers Shaukat and Muhammad Ali and by Abdul Kalam Azad. The movement collapsed in 1924.

q_en: Kazi Nazrul Islam is the national poet of ______.
e_en: Kazi Nazrul Islam is the national poet of Bangladesh. He was a Bengali poet, writer, musician and anti-colonial revolutionary. he produced a large body of poetry and music with themes that included religious devotion and rebellion against oppression. He joined the British Indian Army in 1917. Nazrul wrote and composed about 4,000 songs, known collectively as Nazrul Geeti. He also awarded with Padma Bhushan in 1960.

q_en: Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura became states under ______.
o_en: North Eastern Republic of India Act, 1972
North Eastern Region New State Act, 1972
e_en: Three northeastern states of Tripura, Manipur and Meghalaya celebrate their foundation day. The erstwhile princely states of Tripura and Manipur were merged with India in October 1949 and became full-fledged states on January 21, 1972. Meghalaya was part of Assam before becoming a full-fledged state under the North Eastern Region (Re-Organisation) Act, 1971.

e_en: Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first Indian to be conferred with Ramon Magsaysay Award for his contribution to community leadership. Ramon Magsaysay award, also known as the Nobel Prize of Asia is an annual established in the memory of the former Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay.

q_en: Who among the following is/was the longest serving prime minister of Bangladesh?
e_en: The longest-serving Prime Minister of Bangladesh is Sheikh Hasina. She is a Bangladeshi politician serving as the 10th Prime Minister of Bangladesh, having held the office since January 2009. She is the daughter of Bangladesh's first President Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.

q_en: What is the term used to describe the angular distance of a place north or south of Earth's equator?
e_en: Latitude is defined as the angular distance of a place north or south of Earth's equator. Pole is a point on the either side of the surface of the Earth where lines of longitude meet. The Earth is divided by the 0 degree latitude into equal halves known as Hemisphere. Longitude are defined as the imaginary lines that bisects the globe through the North and South poles.

q_en: When the output is equal to zero, the variable cost is ______.
e_en: When the output is equal to zero, the variable cost is zero. Variable costs are those that depend on the level of output. The fixed costs are those that are present even when production is zero, and therefore the variable cost is zero when output is zero.

q_en: Which of the following is the busiest sea port in Pakistan?
e_en: Karachi Post is the busiest sea port of Pakistan. It handles around 60% of the total cargo of Pakistan. Qasim port is in Sindh province of Pakistan. Keti port is in Sindh province of Pakistan. Gwadar port is situated in Balochistan Province of Pakistan.

q_en: In economic terms what do we mean by 'intermediate goods'?
o_en: Goods sold between industries for the resale or production of other goods
Goods in transit before reaching the consumers
e_en: The correct answer is Option C i.e. Intermediate goods ​ Intermediate goods are the goods sold between industries for the resale or production of other goods. These products are also called semi-finished products because they are used as inputs to become part of the finished products. Examples of intermediate goods are Salt, Sugar, etc.

q_en: As a reaction to Rowlatt Act, _________ was organised as National Humiliation Day.
e_en: 6th April 1919 was organised as National Humiliation day as a reaction to Rowlatt Act. Rowlatt Act was officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Act,1919. It was passed in March 1919 by the Imperial Legislative Council. The Act gave the authority to the Britishers to detain anybody suspected of terrorist activities without any trials.

q_en: Mother Teresa, the founder of 'Missionaries of Charity', was born on _________.
e_en: Mother Teresa was born in Macedonia on 26 August 1910. She was honoured in the Catholic Church as Saint Teresa of Calcutta. She received the Ramon Magsaysay Peace Prize in 1962 and Nobel Peace Prize in 1979. She became the Indian citizen in 1950 and was awarded Bharat Ratna in 1980.

q_en: The 'Tanakh' is the sacred text of which religion/sect?
e_en: The Torah is part of the larger text known as the Tanakh or the Hebrew Bible. ‘The Torah’ is the central reference of Judaism. It has a range of meanings. It can most specifically mean the first five books of the 24 books of the Tanakh, and it usually includes the rabbinic commentaries. It is supplemental oral tradition represented by later texts such as the Midrash and the Talmud.

q_en: Which of the following was a port city of the Indus Valley Civilization?
e_en: Lothal is a port city in Gujarat, located on the banks of the Bhogava River, a right tributary of the Sabarmati River. It had the earliest known dock in the world, used mainly for trade purposes in the Indus Valley Civilization. Lothal is situated in the Ahmedabad District in modern Gujarat. It is considered a port town according to the Archaeological Survey of India.

q_en: The 'Friendship Highway' is a road that connects China to ______.
e_en: The 'Friendship Highway' also known as the China-Nepal Highway, connects the capital of Tibet, Lhasa with the Nepalese-Chinese border between Zhangmu and Kodari. The 800-kilometre long 'Friendship Highway' goes through the Himalayan mountains and along the Yarlung valley upto Shigatse, Tibet's second-largest city and formerly the home of the Panchen Lamas.

q_en: In which year was the 'Battle of Goa' fought?
e_en: Afonso de Albuquerque succeeded Dom Francisco de Almeida as Governor of the Portuguese State of India on November 4, 1509. The Marshal of Portugal Dom Fernando Coutinho, sent by King Manuel had been ordered to enforce the orderly succession of Albuquerque to office. In 1510, the governor of Portuguese India Afonso de Albuquerque captured the city of Goa.

q_en: The Constitution of India was amended for the first time in which year?
e_en: The Constitution of India was amended for the first time on 10th May 1951. The Statement of Objects and Reasons appended to the Constitution (First Amendment) Bill, 1951 was enacted as the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951. The first amendment added Article 15(4) and Article 19(6) and also brought changes in the right to property in pursuance after the decision of Supreme Court regarding Fundamental Right of the Citizens.

q_en: The former princely state of Tripura in the north-eastern part of India was ruled by _________ Dynasty.
e_en: The former princely state of Tripura in the north-eastern part of India was ruled by Manikya dynasty. Ratna Fa was the 145th king of Twipra and he was the first to assume the title Manikya and as such can be considered the founder of the Manikya dynasty. The first king of Twipra is Chandra, the moon himself but the list of historical begins with Ratna Fa only.

q_en: In which province of China is the Huangguoshu National Park located which houses the world's largest waterfall cluster.
e_en: Huangguoshu National Park of China is located in west Guizhou province. It is 128 km from Guiyang and 45 km from Anshun, a tourist destination in West China. Huangguoshu is also the largest waterfalls in China and East Asia located on the Baishui River in Anshun in the same province.

q_en: About 70% of the sun is made up of ______.
e_en: Sun is the most hot glowing sphere of Plasma at the centre of the solar system. It is made of gases and most of it is hydrogen (about 70%) and helium (about 28%). While carbon, nitrogen and oxygen make up 1.5% and the other 0.5% is made up of other elements like neon, iron, silicon, magnesium and sulfur. It is one of most important sources of energy for life on earth.

q_en: World Water Day is annually celebrated on ______.
e_en: World Water Day is celebrated annually on 22nd March. The day aims to draw attention to the importance of universal access to clean water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) facilities in developing countries. The day also focuses on advocating for the sustainable management of freshwater resources. Theme: "Leaving no one behind".

e_en: The bollywood film 'Kai Po Che' was based on Chetan Bhagat's novel 'The 3 Mistakes of My Life' released in 2013. It was directed by Abhishek Kapoor and Pubali Chaudhari, Supratik Sen, Abhishek Kapoor and Chetan Bhagat were the screenplay writers of the film. The film had received 6 nominations at the 59th Filmfare Awards and it won two awards, including Best Screenplay for Kapoor and Best Background Score for Hitesh Sonik.

q_en: Which Indian author wrote the book 'The English Teacher'?
e_en: The English Teacher is a 1945 novel written by R. K. Narayan. It is the third and final part in the 'Malgudi Days" series, preceded by Swami and Friends (1935) and The Bachelor of Arts (1937). This novel, dedicated to Narayan's wife Rajam is not only autobiographical but also poignant in its intensity of feeling. The story is a series of experiences in the life of Krishna, an English teacher, and his quest towards achieving inner peace and self - development.

q_en: The interest rate charged by banks on short-term loans to their largest, most secure and most creditworthy customers is called ______.
e_en: Benchmark prime lending rate or ;prime rate is the interest rate that commercial banks charge their most creditworthy customers. Prime lending rate, is largely determined by the federal funds rate, which is the overnight rate that banks use to lend to one another. The prime rate is also important for individual borrowers, as the prime rate directly affects the lending rates available for a mortgage, small business loan or personal loan.

q_en: Who among the following is the only Indian to have won the Amateur World title in both, snooker and billiards?
e_en: Pankaj Advani is the only Indian to have won the Amateur World title in both, snooker and billiards. He is the only snooker player to ever win professional world titles in both the long and short formats of snooker and both formats of English billiards. Pankaj Advani has also won country's most prestigious awards Padma Shri in 2009, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2006 and Arjuna Award in 2004.

q_en: When was the Constitution of Pakistan enforced?
e_en: The National Assembly of Pakistan passed it's Constitution on 10th April, 1973. The President of the constituent Assembly authenticated it on 12th April 1973 and the Assembly published the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. After partitioned from India, Pakistan was declared as an Islamic Republic and it was made mandatory that only a Muslim could become the President of the country.

q_en: Which one of the following is the highest altitude lake of Pakistan?
e_en: The highest lake in Pakistan is the Rush Lake located in Nagar Valley, Gilgit - Baltistan at an altitude of over 4,700 meters near the Rush Pari Peak. It is also the 25th highest lake is the world. The second highest lake in Pakistan is the Karambar Lake, which at an altitude of 4,272 meters, is the 31st highest lake in the world. It is also one of the highest alpine lakes in the world.

q_en: _______ assumed the title of 'Gangaikondachola', or the conqueror of the river Ganga.
e_en: Indian king Rajendra Chola-I used naval powers to conquer parts of Eastasia. He defeated Sri Vijaya or the Kadaram kingdom in East Asia and bore the title Kadaramkonda. He belongs to the Imperial Chola Dynasty. His reign was from 1012-1044 A.D. He built a city called Gangaikonda Cholapuram to commemorate his victory in his northern India campaign which spanned up to Ganges River, where he defeated Bengal king Mahipala-I.

e_en: The University Grants Commission (UGC) was formally established in the year 1956. It provides funds for the colleges and universities which are government-recognised. It is headquartered in New Delhi and has 6 regional centres.

q_en: Which country in the world has the largest number of international borders?
e_en: China and Russia have the largest number of international borders. Both have 14 neighbouring countries. The neighbouring countries of China include Mongolia, Russia, Kazakhstan, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Bhutan, Nepal, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos, and North Korea. The neighbouring countries of Russia include Ukraine, Belarus, Latvia, Estonia, Finland, Norway, North Korea, China, Georgia, Mongolia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Lithuania and Poland.

q_en: Which of the followings is the national bird of China?
e_en: Red-crowned Crane is the national bird of China. Grand Cayman Parrot is the national bird of Cayman Islands. Robin is the national bird of Bangladesh. Barn Swallow is the national bird of Austria.

q_en: The term 'Blood Moon' is used to refer to ________.
e_en: The term 'Blood Moon' is used to refer to Lunar Eclipse since the moon takes on a reddish tinge when it is fully eclipsed. A lunar eclipse occurs when the moon travels through the umbra of the earth and blocks all direct sunlight. A solar eclipse occurs when the new moon comes between the earth and the sun, thus blocking the sun rays.

q_en: When the fiscal deficit is high, what happens to the prices?
o_en: There is no direct impact on the prices
e_en: When the fiscal deficit is high, there is no direct impact on the prices. When the government spends more money than what it earned during the fiscal year, then it is known as fiscal deficit.

q_en: What is the value of all tangible resources such as raw materials and labour that are used in the production process called?
e_en: The value of all tangible resources such as raw materials and labour that are used in the production process is called real cost. A fixed cost is that which does not change with a decrease or increase in the amount of services or goods sold or produced. Opportunity Costs are the benefits that an investor or individual misses out when choosing one alternative over other. Variable Costs are corporate expenses which change in proportion to production output.

q_en: The traditional art of 'Jamdani' weaving originated in ________.
e_en: The traditional art of 'Jamdani' weaving originated in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The Jamdani sarees are also known as Dhakai sarees. Jam means flower and dani means vase. Its earliest mention is found in Arthshastra which dates back to 3rd century BC. The art bloomed the most during the Mughal Period.

q_en: The river Ganga emerges from Gangotri Glacier and ends at ________.
e_en: The river Ganga emerges from Gangotri Glacier and ends at Bay of Bengal. Ganges is the longest river of India. It is 2,525 km long. Its tributaries include Yamuna, Gandak, Ramganga, Son, Ghaghra, Gomti, Kosi, Tamsa, Punpun, and Mahananda.

q_en: Burma became independent soverign republic in the year ________.
e_en: Burma became an independent sovereign republic on 4 January 1948. Burma was colonized by Britain in the 19th century. It got free from the UK on this day. The country is bordered by India, China, Laos, and Thailand.

q_en: Who is the first Indian national to win the 'Sri Lanka Rathna' award?
e_en: Narasimhan Ram is the first Indian national to win the 'Sri Lanka Rathna' award. He was awarded on 14 November 2005. He is an Indian journalist and also served as the MD of The Hindu till 2012. The award is the highest national honour conferred by Sri Lanka to the non-nationals.

q_en: In which year did the Indian Premier League (IPL) start?
e_en: The Indian Premier League (IPL) began in the year 2008 and was founded by BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India). It is a 20-20 cricket league which is held every year in the month of April-May. Mumbai Indians were the winner of the IPL 2019 held in Hyderabad. Currently, there are a total of 10 teams playing in the IPL(2022).

q_en: Who among the following was given the title 'Quaid-i-Azam'?
e_en: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was given the title 'Quaid-i-Azam'. Quaid-i-Azam means Great Leader. He was also known by the name Baba-i-Quam, which means The Father of the Nation. He served as the leader of All-Indian Muslim League and also as the Governor-General of Pakistan.

q_en: Who presides over the joint sitting of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?
e_en: The correct answer is Speaker of Lok Sabha.

q_en: Mitra Mela was a revolutionary organisation founded by Vinayak Savarkar in the year ________.
e_en: Mitra Mela was a revolutionary organisation founded by Vinayak Savarkar in the year 1899 in Nashik. He, along with his brother Ganesh Savarkar established the society. It is now known by the name Abhinav Bharat Society or the Young India Society. Vinayak Savarkar was a politician, lawyer, writer, and an independence activist.

q_en: A _______ is not constrained by prior work.
e_en: A greenfield project is not constrained by prior work. These are constructed on unused lands where there is not any need to demolish or remodel an existing structure. Some of its examples are airports, power plants, or factories built from scratch. A strategic alliance is an agreement between 2 parties, wherein, they undertake a mutually beneficial project and both retain their independence.

q_en: Which one of the following is the deepest gorge in the world?
e_en: Kali Gandaki Gorge is the deepest gorge in the world. It is situated in Nepal. Its upper part is known as Thak Khola. Garganta del Cares is situated in Spain. Vikos Gorge is situated in Greece. Tiger Leaping Gorge is situated in China.

q_en: British East India Company defeated the Portuguese in the ___________.
e_en: The correct answer is Battle of Suvali​. In 1612 the East India Company's ships defeated the Portuguese in the Swally estuary off Surat. The naval Battle of Swally, also known as Battle of Suvali, took place on 29–30 November 1612 off the coast of Suvali a village near the Surat city and was a victory for four English East India Company galleons over four Portuguese galleons.

q_en: How many provinces are there in Sri Lanka?
e_en: There are a total of 9 provinces and 25 states in Sri Lanka. These were created in 1987 by the 13th Amendment of the Sri Lankan Constitution. These 9 provinces are Central, Eastern, North Central, Northern, North Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, Uva, and Western.

q_en: In India, which of the following article of the Constitution of India provides for the formation of a new state?
e_en: Article 3 of the Constitution of India provides for the formation of a new state. Article 1 states that India shall be a union of states. Article 9 deals with the law of Indian nationality. Article 2 states that the Parliament may add or establish new states into the union of India.

q_en: Identify the national sport of Sri Lanka.
e_en: Volleyball is the national sport of Sri Lanka. Basketball is the national sport of Estonia. Cricket is the national sport of Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, Barbados, Grenada, Guyana, and Jamaica

q_en: Sir Thomas Roe visited the court of Mughal ruler _______ as the ambassador of the king of England.
e_en: Sir Thomas Roe visited the court of Mughal ruler Jahangir as the ambassador of the king of England, in 1615. He lived as a resident of Agra till 1619. He was an English diplomat of the Jacobean and the Elizabethan period. He compiled a work titled Journal of the Mission to the Mogul Empire.

q_en: Which Indian author wrote the book 'Two Lives'?
e_en: Vikram Seth is the author of the book 'Two Lives'. Amish Tripathi The Immortals of Meluha Vikram Seth Two Lives Chetan Bhagat Revolution 2020 Amitava Ghosh Sea of Poppies

q_en: A marketplace in which a final good or service is bought and sold is called ________.
e_en: The correct answer is Option D i.e. Product Market. A marketplace in which a final good or service is bought and sold is called Product Market. A factor market is where the companies purchase what they need to produce their services and goods. A commodity market is a virtual or physical marketplace for selling, buying, and trading primary or raw products. The equity market is for trading equity instruments. It is also known as the stock market.

q_en: Opium wars were fought between the British and ________.
e_en: Opium wars were fought between the British and China. The war took place in the mid-19th century. The first one was held between China and British in 1839-42. The second one was fought between France and Britain against China in 1856-60.

q_en: Who among the following was the first Chinese to receive the Nobel Prize for literature?
e_en: Mo Yan was the first Chinese to receive the Nobel Prize for literature in the year 2012. His first work was published in the year 1981. He is also the 109th recipient of the award. Some of his acclaimed works include Big Breasts and Wide Hips and Republic of Wine.

q_en: Bihar Diwas is annually celebrated on ________ to commemorate the day Bihar was carved out from the Bengal Presidency.
e_en: Bihar Diwas is annually celebrated on 22 March to commemorate the day Bihar was carved out from the Bengal Presidency. It was on this day in 1912 that the state was finally carved out. March 22, 2019 was the 107th foundation day of Bihar. The day was first celebrated on a long-scale in 2010.

q_en: Rule ________ (of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha) does NOT involve a formal motion before the Parliament House, hence no voting can take place after discussion on matters under this rule.
e_en: Rule 193 (of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha) does not involve a formal motion before the Parliament House, hence no voting can take place after the discussion on matters under this rule. Rule 184 allows voting but rule 193 doesn't. Lok Sabha is the lower house of the Parliament, while Rajya Sabha is the upper house.

q_en: _______ gases trap heat in the atmosphere which makes the Earth warmer, causing global warming.
e_en: Greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere which makes the Earth warmer, causing global warming. Greenhouse effect is a process that occurs when the temperature of the Earth traps the sun's heat and this, in result, makes the earth much warmer. Global warming occurs when greenhouse gases, carbon dioxide and other pollutants collect in the atmosphere and absorb solar radiations and sunlight.

q_en: A scientific study of rocks that deals with their composition, texture and structure; their occurrence and distribution; and their origin in relation to physicochemical conditions is called ________.
e_en: A scientific study of rocks that deals with their composition, texture and structure; their occurrence and distribution; and their origin in relation to physicochemical conditions is called petrology. Lithology is the study of the general physical characteristics of rocks. Geology is the study of earth, its structure, materials with which it is made and other processes related to it.

q_en: Tipu Sultan and British East India Company signed the Treaty of Mangalore in the year _______.
e_en: Tipu Sultan and British East India Company signed the Treaty of Mangalore in the year 1784. It brought an end to the 2nd Anglo-Mysore war. Tipu Sultan was the ruler of the Mysore Kingdom. The Second Anglo-Mysore War took place from 1780-84 between the British East India Company and the Mysore Kingdom.

q_en: Which of the following is the longest river in Pakistan that originates from Lake Manasarovar?
e_en: Indus is the longest river in Pakistan that originates from Lake Manasarovar. In terms of annual water flow, it is the 21st largest river of the world. It is also known as Pakistan's lifeline and is 3,180 km long. Sutlej river flows through northern India and Pakistan and is a tributary of the river Indus. Kabul river originates in Afghanistan. Chenab is one of the 5 major rivers of Punjab and flows through India and Pakistan.

q_en: Which of the following is the largest container port of India?
e_en: The Jawaharlal Nehru Port is the largest container port in India. It is located in Navi Mumbai. The port alone handles about 40% of the countries ocean cargo. The port serves as the major cargo hub for Karnataka, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra.

q_en: Which theory in economics proposes that countries export what they can most efficiently and plentifully produce?
e_en: The Heckscher-Ohlin Model proposes that countries export what they can produce very efficiently and in high quantities. It is also popularly known as the H-O Model or 2x2x2 model. It is used to examine the trade equilibrium between two countries. It takes into consideration that countries should ideally export materials and resources of which they have an excess, while proportionately importing those resources they need.

q_en: Who is the author of the book The Buddha and His Dhamma?
e_en: Buddha and His Dhamma was authored by B R Ambedkar. B R Ambedkar or Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was a famous Indian social reformer. He also inspired the Dalit Movement in India. Buddha and His Dhamma were one of his last works published in 1957 after his death which took place on 6 December 1956.

q_en: Who among the following is/was the longest serving governor of an Indian state?
e_en: M M Jacob has served the longest number of days as governor of an Indian state. He was the governor of Meghalaya. He served for a total of 11 years 293 days from 1995 to 2007. Next in line is Padmaja Naidu who served in West Bengal for 10 years 209 days from 1956 to 1967. Followed by N N Vohra who served in Jammu and Kashmir for 10 years and 59 days from 2008 to 2018.

q_en: Which of the following is the national sport of Bangladesh?
e_en: Kabaddi is the national sport of Bangladesh. Despite that, cricket and football are much more popular in the country. Kabaddi is also known as Ha-Du-Du in the country. It is said that Kabaddi was decided as the national sport by the leaders of the country to break away from the colonial roots as both cricket and football are very famous British sports.

q_en: How many sessions of the Lok Sabha are normally held in a year?
e_en: There are 3 sessions of the Lok Sabha held annually. Budget Session February to May Monsoon Session July to September Winter Session November to Mid December During the sessions, the timings of the Lok Sabha are from 11 AM to 1 PM and 2 PM to 6 PM. The timings may extend beyond depending on the topics at hand on some days.

q_en: With which sport is the term bleeder associated?
e_en: The term bleeder is associated with boxing. It is a slang term used to describe a player that bleeds or gets cut very easily. Some other common terminologies for the sports are as follows Sport Terms Swimming Back Stroke Freestyle, Butterfly,Breast stroke (all are swimming styles) Cricket Toss, Run, Wicket, Pitch, Stump, Bails, Crease Volleyball Spikers , Service , Love. & nbsp;

q_en: Who among the following was the last Nawab of Awadh?
e_en: The correct answer is Wajid Ali Shah. Wajid Ali Shah was the eleventh and last King of Awadh. Lord Dalhousie, Governor General of British India, had deposed him under the pretext of misgovernance in February 1856. Wajid Ali Shah's first wife was Alam Ara who was better known as Khas Mahal ( transl. special wife). Begum Hazrat Mahal, also known as the Begum of Awadh, was the second wife of Nawab of Awadh Wajid Ali Shah.​

q_en: Who was the first Russian prime minister to visit independent India?
e_en: Nikolai Bulganin was the first Russian Prime Minister to visit India after independence. The Prime Minister visited India in 1955. He was accompanied by Nikita Khruschev who was the Secretary of the Communist Party. They travelled to Punjab, Bombay, Bangalore, Madras and Calcutta and also some smaller towns.

q_en: In which year was the Battle of Saragarhi fought?
e_en: The famous Battle of Saragarhi was fought on 12 September of 1897. The battle took place in Tirah which is in present-day Pakistan. It was fought between The British Indian Empire and Afghan tribesmen of the area. Only 21 Sikh soldiers fought for the British against about 10,000 tribesmen. The Sikh soldiers lost but fought till their deaths as a last stand.

q_en: Byopa is a traditional headgear of tribes belonging to ______.
e_en: The Byopa is traditionally worn by tribals of Arunachal Pradesh It is mainly worn by people of the Nyishi tribe The cap is mainly made of cane and is a warriors headgear to protect the head in war

q_en: Chepu is a unique cultural symbol of ______.
e_en: Chepu is a prominent Nepali cultural symbol. It is a decorative deity that is also known as the guardian of the house. It is believed in Nepali culture that it wards off evil spirits. Chepu is also known as Kirtikmukha or 'face of glory'.

q_en: Which of the following is the highest peak in Sri Lanka?
e_en: The correct answer is Mount Pedro. Pidurutalagala peak is also known as the Mount Pedro peak. It has a height of 2524 meters or 8281 feet above sea level. The peak is used as the central communications array of the Government of Sri Lanka and armed forces. It also serves as an important point in the country's radar system.

q_en: Which state of India was ruled by the Ahom Dynasty?
e_en: The Ahom dynasty ruled over present-day Assam. The dynasty ruled over Assam for almost 6 centuries from 1228 to 1826. The founder of the Ahom dynasty was Sukhapaa who came from Mong Mao, Mong Mao was a small medieval state located on present-day Myanmar-China border. The rule of the dynasty ended in the Burmese invasion of Assam in 1826.

q_en: Which theory is used to make long-run predictions about exchange rates in a flexible exchange rate system?
e_en: The Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) Theory can make long term predictions about exchange rates in a flexible exchange rate system. Basically PPP compares the economic productivity and standards of living of countries to predict exchange rates between different currencies.

q_en: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act was passed in the year _______.
e_en: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act was passed in the year 2006. It regulates and classifies enterprises as small, medium, and micro enterprises. It classifies MSMEs on the basis of investment in equipment and plant and machinery. Nitin Gadkari is the Minister of MSME currently.

q_en: The movement of the local farmers of Bardoli in Gujarat against the British in 1928 was led by _______.
e_en: The movement of the local farmers of Bardoli in Gujarat against the British in 1928 was led by Vallabhbhai Patel. It was done against the unjust raising of taxes. It is considered as a major revolt of the Indian Independence Movement. Its success gave rise to Vallabhbhai Patel, thus making him one of the important leaders of the Indian freedom struggle.

q_en: The Khadi and village Industries Commission Act was passed in the year _______.
e_en: The Khadi and village Industries Commission Act was passed in the year 1956. Through this Act, a statutory body was established- Khadi and Village Industries Commission. It works under the Ministry of MSME and aims to organise, promote and plan the development and establishment of khadi industries in the rural areas.

q_en: Who was the first Indian to win the Miss Universe title?
e_en: Sushmita Sen was the first Indian to win the Miss Universe title. She won the pageant in the year 1994. She was also crowned Miss India in the year 1994. Reita Faria was the first Indian and Asian to win the Miss World title in 1966. Madhu Sapre won the Miss India title in 1992. Persis Khambatta won the Miss India title in 1965.

q_en: Name the oldest operating port in India built by the British East India Company.
e_en: Kolkata Port is the oldest operating port in India built by the British East India Company. There are a total of 12 major ports in India. Chennai Port is the third oldest and second largest port of India. Mumbai port is owned by the Government of India. The second largest port by volume of cargo handled is the Vishakapatnam Port.

q_en: The East India Company sent Captain William Hawkins to the court of Emperor _______ in 1608 to seek permission to open a factory at Surat.
e_en: The East India Company sent Captain William Hawkins to the court of Emperor Jahangir in 1608 to seek permission to open a factory at Surat. He was well versed with Turkish and Jahangir also knew some of it since it was the native tongue of Mughal Emperor Babur. He was called 'English Khan' by Jahangir. William Hawkins was the commander of Hector, the first ship of the British East India Company to anchor at Surat in 1608.

q_en: The approximate diameter of the sun is _______ times the diameter of Earth.
e_en: The approximate diameter of the sun is 109 times the diameter of Earth. The sun contains 99.86% of all the mass of the solar system. The weight of the sun is 333,000 times as much as Earth. It is 864,400 miles across.

q_en: What was the historical name of the city of Guwahati?
e_en: Pragjyotishpur was the historical name of the city of Guwahati. Under the Kamarupa kingdom, it used to be the capital of Assam. Durjaya was the ancient name for North Guwahati. Guwahati lies on the foothills of the Shillong plateau and between the banks of the river Brahmaputra. It is one of the largest cities of Assam.

q_en: _______ was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India.
e_en: Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India, who served from 1950-1958. The CEC is appointed by the President of India. He has a tenure of up to 65 years or 6 years. He is usually a member of the IAS or Indian Civil Service. The current Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India is Sh. Rajiv Kumar, who took office on 15th May 2022.

q_en: _______ is the hottest planet in the solar system.
e_en: Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system. The temperature on Venus reaches around 465 degrees Celsius, which is hot enough to melt lead. It is the second planet from the sun and is named after a Roman Goddess. Earth and Venus are called twins since they are the same in size, density, and mass. The coldest planet of the solar system is Uranus.

q_en: Name the westernmost point of India.
e_en: Guhar Moti is the westernmost point of India. It is a small village located in the Kutch district of Gujarat. The northernmost point of India is located in the eastern Karakoram range in the Himalayas, near Indira Col, Siachen Glacier. The easternmost point is Kibithu in Arunachal Pradesh. Indira Point in Great Nicobar Island is the southernmost point.

q_en: During the Sao Joao festivities, Goans present _______ to each other.
e_en: During the Sao Joao festivities, Goans present fruits to each other. The Sao Joao festival is celebrated in Goa to pay tribute to St. John the Baptist. It is held at the beginning of monsoon, on June 24. St. John was the relative of Mother Mary.

q_en: The 'Instrument of Surrender' which ended the Portuguese rule in India was signed on _______.
e_en: The 'Instrument of Surrender' which ended the Portuguese rule in India was signed on 19th December 1961. This ended 450 years of Portuguese in India. Francisco de Almeida was the first Viceroy of the Portuguese state and its headquarter was Cochin. The movement to end the Portuguese rule was called the Goa Liberation Movement.

q_en: Name the smallest district in India.
e_en: By area, Mahe in Puducherry is the smallest district in India. The district is spread across an area of 9 sq km. As per 2001 census, it has a population of 36,000, while the population density is 4091 sq. km. Kutch in Gujarat is the largest district of India in terms of area. Leh is the second largest district of India.

q_en: Which of the following is NOT a part of the 'Char Dham Yatra' in North India?
e_en: Vaishno Devi is not a part of the 'Char Dham Yatra' in North India. The temple is located in Katra in Jammu. Char Dham comprise of 4 pilgrimage sites in North India, in the state of Uttarakhand. These are Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath, and Badrinath. Char Dham of India are Rameswaram, Puri, Dwarka, and Badrinath.

q_en: ​Prolific Indian painter Maqbool Fida Husain predominantly used which of these animals to depict a lively and free spirit in his paintings?
e_en: The correct answer is option B: MF Husain has portrayed a number of paintings depicting horses. Maqbool Fida Husain (1915 - 2011): Popularly known as MF Husain, he is one of the greatest artists of the 20th century. He started his painting career in Zurich in 1952 through exhibitions. He was also entitled to 'Picasso of India' by Forbes magazine.</l

q_en: ​The ruins of the ancient city of Hampi - capital of Vijayanagara - is located in which present day Indian state?
e_en: The correct answer is Karnataka ​The ruins of the ancient city of Hampi is a historical site located in Karnataka. It is a UNESCO world heritage site and was granted that status in the year 1986. It was established as Vidyanagar by Harihara and Buka, the founders of the Sangama dynasty, in the memory of their guru Vidyaranya. Ancient temples, ruins of forts, and aquatic structures are the major attractions. Temples related to Hinduism as well as Buddhism are found here.

q_en: Sir Thomas Roe came as an official ambassador from King James I of England to which Mughal emperor's court?
e_en: The correct answer is option B: Sir Thomas Roe visited the court of Emperor Jahangir in 1615 as an ambassador of King James I. Expelled Portuguese from Hoogli. His reign was called the Golden age of Mughal Architecture. Taj Mahal. Red fort. Jama Masjid. Sheesh Mahal.

q_en: In which year Sanchi was discovered after being abandoned for nearly 600 Years?
e_en: Option C is the correct answer: Sanchi was rediscovered after 600 years by Bengal Cavalry of Britishers in 1818. The discovery is attributed to General Henry Taylor. The town of Sanchi, the abode of one of the principal Buddhist sites is located in the state of Madhya Pradesh. The Buddhist monuments there

q_en: Which of the following books is NOT written by Salman Rushdie?
e_en: The correct answer is option B: 'An Area of Darkness' is written by VS Naipaul. Book Details Midnight's Children By Salman Rushdie Published in 1981. Talks about pre and post Independence events. An Area of Darkness By VS Naipaul Published in 1964. A travelogue that throws light on conditions prevailing in India in the early sixties. The Satanic Verses By Salman Rushdie Published in 1988. A work of fiction that used magical realism. Shame By Salman Rushdie Published in 1983.

q_en: The Araku Valley, a tourist resort, is located near which of these cities of South India?
e_en: The correct answer is Visakhapatnam. </strong&g

q_en: What is the uniform GST rate that has been fixed up for lottery prizes by the GST Council?
e_en: The correct answer is 40%. On February 24, 2020, through a notification of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes, all the lotteries were brought under the tax slab of 40%. All the lotteries whether State-run or with private ownership will now fall under this uniform tax rate. Goods and Services Tax: It is an indirect tax that was introduced on

q_en: ​For which of the following sports was Dronavalli Harika, conferred with the prestigious Padma Shri award?
e_en: The correct answer is chess. She has won three bronze medals at the Women's World Chess Championship of 2012, 2015, and 2017. She was honored with the Arjuna award in the year 2007 - 08. She also won the FIDE Women's Grand Prix in 2016. In 2019 she was conferred with Padma Shri.

q_en: Veteran freedom fighter, social reformer and feminist Savithribai Phule hailed from which of the following states of India?
e_en: Option D is the correct answer: Savithribai Phule belongs to Maharashtra. She was born on January 3, 1831, and was married to Jyotirao Phule. Her husband decided to educate her in order to elevate the status of women. She is a social reformer and worked a lot for women empowerment. After the completion of her education, she opened a girl's school at Vishrambag, Pune. She started teaching there and is known as the first female teacher of India.

q_en: The World Food Program (WFP) is the food assistance branch of the United Nations. Where is it headquartered?
e_en: Option C is the correct answer: World Food Programme is a branch of the United Nations and is based in Rome, Italy. It was established in 1961 and aims at eradicating world hunger aiding people with food assistance during a humanitarian crisis. It is a member of the United Nations Development Programme. Structure: It is governed by representatives from 36 member states of the UN or FAO. David Beasley is the current executive director of WFP and heads it.

q_en: Which of these institutions fixes the Repo Rate and the Reverse Repo Rate in India?
o_en: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
e_en: The correct answer is option D: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is responsible for fixing Repo or Reverse Repo Rate. RBI regulates these rates as a part of its monetary policy. Monetary policy refers to the steps undertaken by the central bank to control the liquidity and supply of money in the market. Repo Rate: It is an Acronym for the Repurchasing Agreement Rate. It is the rate at which RBI lends money to other banks in the country for the short term.

q_en: ​Kolathunadu, Valluvanad and Thekkumkoor were ancient small-time kingdoms in which state of India?
e_en: Option B is the correct answer: ​Kolathunadu, Valluvanad, and Thekkumkoor were the feudal kingdoms of Kerela. Kingdom Features Kolathunadu The Area between Perumba and Putupattanam rivers. Kolathiris was the ruling family. Thekkumkoor Founder: Ilayi Raja. Region between Meenachil and Pamban rivers. Emerged after the culmination of the Chera Kalusekhara dynasty. Vennimala was their first Capital. Valluvanad The region between the Nila river and Panthaloor Hills.

q_en: Ajatashatru, a ruler of the Haryanka Dynasty, was the son of _____.
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option A i.e Bimbisara. Bimbisara: Bimbisara was the founder of the Haryanka Dynasty. He was a contemporary of Buddha. He started the policy of annexation and expansion. He was succeeded by his son Ajatashatru. Ajatashatru: He followed a more serious and aggressive policy of expansion. He won the long war with the Kosala in the form of a marriage alliance with the daughter of the Kosala king. Ajatashatru was succeeded by Udayin.

q_en: Which of the following festivals means 'Merry making of the Gods'?
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option A i.e Lai Haraoba. Festival Description Lai Haraoba Lai Haraoba festival is celebrated by the Meitei community to please "Umang Lai" (sacred tree). It is widely celebrated in the state of Manipur in the month of May. Lai Haraoba means 'Merry making of the Gods'. Diwali It is known as "Festival of Lights". it is celebrated in India and as well as other parts of the world.

q_en: In which district of Karnataka is the Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary located?
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option C i.e Kodagu. Wildlife Sanctuary District Adichunchanagiri Wildlife Sanctuary Melukote Temple Wildlife Sanctuary Mandya District, Karnataka Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary It is situated on the border between Wayanad of Kerala on the south and Kodagu of Karnataka in North. It is a part of western ghats.

q_en: Who among the following was the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty?
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option C i.e Dhanananda. Nanda Dynasty: It was founded by Mahapadma Nanda around 467 BC. He Accepted the title of Ekrat meaning the sole sovereign who destroyed all other ruling princes. Dhanananda was the last ruler of the Nanda Dynasty, was overthrown by Chandra Gupta Maurya. During Dhanananda, Alexander attacked India and another King Porus fought against Alexander on the banks of river Jhelum i.e Battle of Hydaspes.

q_en: Archaeologist R Nagaswamy was honoured at the Silver Jubilee International Conference of Art by which country?
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option C i.e Bangladesh. Archaeologist R. Nagaswamy He was honored at the Silver Jubilee International Conference of Art held in Dhaka by Bangladesh<

q_en: Borra caves are situated on the East Coast of India in which of the following hills?
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option A i.e Ananthagiri Hill. Borra Ananthagiri Hill Borra caves: They are located on the East Coast of India, in the Ananthagiri hills of Araku Valley of Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh They are also called Borra Guhalu. Nallamala Hills These are also called as Nallamala Range and are section of Eastern Ghats. They spread across several districts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

q_en: In which of the following states is the Madhavpur Mela celebrated?
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option D i.e Gujarat. Bihar Sonepur Cattle Fair Uttar Pradesh Ramnavmi Mela Deva Mela Madhya Pradesh Ujjain Kumbh Mela Gujarat Madhavpur Mela: Madhavpur lies on the seashore, close to Porbandar and the site is marked by the Madhavrai Temple. The festival associated with the Mela is " Ram Navami".

q_en: Who among the following was honoured after completing the 50th year in the film industry with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
e_en: The Correct Answer is Amitabh Bachchan. Kamal Haasan Padma Bhushan Padma Shri Ordre des Arts et des Lettres (France) Amitabh Bachchan 50th Dadasaheb Phalke Award The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in cinema. It is presented annually by the Directorate of Film Festivals at the National Film Awards ceremony.

q_en: Objects that shine in the night sky are known as:
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option D i.e celestial bodies. Celestial bodies: The sun, the moon, and all those objects shining in the night sky are called celestial bodies. Some celestial bodies are very big and hot. They are made up of gases. They have their own heat and light, which they emit in large amounts. These celestial bodies are called stars. The sun is a star Planets: Some celestial bodies do not have their own heat and light. They are lit by the light of the stars.

q_en: Asia's largest wholesale spice market is located in _______.
e_en: Asia's largest wholesale spice market is located in Delhi. Delhi’s Khari Baoli is Asia’s largest spice market. A wide variety of both local and exotic spices can be found trading here every day. It is located on the western end of Chandni Chowk, close to the Red Fort and adjacent to the Jama Masjid. It came into being during the 17th century, dating back to the Mughal era.

q_en: King Harshavardhana ascended the throne of Thaneshwar and Kannauj on the death of his brother, ________.
e_en: King Harshavardhana ascended the throne of Thaneshwar and Kannauj on the death of his brother, Rajyavardhana. Harsha ascended the throne with the commencement of the 7th century, around 606 AD. By 612 AD Harshavardhana consolidated his kingdom in northern India. Harshavardhana is well known for his religious toleration, able administration and diplomatic relations.

q_en: _________ was the capital of Magadha before the 4th century BCE.

e_en: Depreciation is an annual allowance for wear and tear of a capital good. In other words, it is the cost of the good divided by a number of years of its useful life. While calculating depreciation unexpected or sudden destruction or disuse of capital as can happen with accidents, natural calamities or other such extraneous circumstances are not taken into account.

q_en: The headquarters of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is located in ______.
e_en: The Correct answer is Mumbai. The headquarters of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is located at Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) was formed in December 1928 as 'Provisional' Board of Control'. Important domestic cricket tournaments: Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy, Deodhar Trophy, Vijay Hazare Trophy, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, Irani Cup, etc.

q_en: ______ renounced his knight hood in protest for Jalianwalla Bagh mass killing.
e_en: Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest for Jalianwalla Bagh mass killing. Rabindranath Tagore was awarded a knighthood in 1915 but in 1919 he repudiated it. Jalianwalla Bagh massacre took place on 13th April 1919 in Punjab province of British India. Brigadier-General Dyer directed British Indian Army troops to open fire on unarmed Indian civilians gathered for the Baisakhi festival in Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar.

q_en: The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) was formed by insertion of Article ______ in the Constitution of India.
e_en: National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) was established in 1993 as a statutory body. The 102ⁿd Amendment Act of 2018 inserted Article 338-B and gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC). The primary objective of the commission is to provide the constitutional and other legal safeguards of the socially and educationally backward classes.

q_en: Which National Park among the following is the largest protected area in the Eastern Himalayan sub-region?
e_en: The correct answer is Namdapha National Park. Namdapha National Park is the largest protected area in the Eastern Himalayan sub-region. It is a wide protected area of 1,985 km² in Arunachal Pradesh of Northeast India. The national park harbours the northernmost lowland evergreen rainforests in the world at 27°N latitude. Even harbours vast dipterocarp forests, covering the northwestern parts of the eco-region rainforests Mizoram-Manipur-Kachin.

q_en: In terms of area, which state has the largest forest cover in India?
e_en: In terms of area, Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover in India. It is the second-largest state by area after Rajasthan in India, and the fifth-largest state by population. The capital of Madhya Pradesh is Bhopal. The largest city of Madhya Pradesh is Indore. As per the economy, it is the 10th largest state economy in India. Notes: Area-wise Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover in the country followed by Arunachal Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Maharashtra.

q_en: Which dynasty built the pancha rathas of Mahabalipuram?
e_en: Pallava dynasty built the Pancha rathas of Mahabalipuram. This was an Indian dynasty, which ruled a portion of southern India from 275 CE to 897 CE. Since the extinction of the Satavahana dynasty which the Pallavas served as feudatories, they gained prominence. During the reign of Mahendravarman I (571–630 CE), and Narasimhavarman I (630–668 CE) it became a major power. Pallavas built the Shore Temple in Mamallapuram, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q_en: ​Which of the following rivers flows through Tiruttani a famous pilgrimage place of South India?
e_en: Nandi river flows through Tiruttani a famous pilgrimage place of South India. Tiruttani is a town located in Tamil Nadu. This city is famous for the Temple of Tiruthani Murugan, one of the Arupadaiveedu, dedicated to Kartikeya. When Andhra state was established on 1 November 1953, Tirutani was part of Andhra Pradesh state's Chittoor district until 1960.

q_en: ​In which year was the Nahargarh Fort built in Jaipur by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II?
e_en: ​In 1734, the Nahargarh Fort was built in Jaipur by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II. He was the ruler of the Amber kingdom. He founded the Jaipur city and made it capital. In 1699, the Mughal Emperor, Aurangzeb, who had summoned him to Delhi impressed by his intellect, gave him the title of Sawaii. The Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah awarded him the title of Saramad-i-Rajaha-i-Hind on 21 April 1721.

q_en: ​As per the government rules, how much percentage of advance tax needs to be paid by 15th June by an individual who is liable to pay advance tax?
e_en: ​As per the government rules, 15% of advance tax needs to be paid by 15th June by an individual who is liable to pay advance tax. Advance tax means earnings tax will be charged in advance, rather than lump-sum payment at year-end. The way you collect tax is also known as earn tax. Such payments are to be made in installments as given by the income tax department according to the due dates.

q_en: ​In which year was the Currency Building in the BBD Bagh or Dalhousie area of Kolkata constructed?
e_en: ​In 1833, the Currency Building was constructed in the BBD Bagh or Dalhousie area of Kolkata. It is also one of the country's oldest buildings that had functioned as a bank. It operated as Reserve Bank of India (RBI), as the name implies, after which it deteriorated till 2002. It has been designated a protected monument by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

q_en: In which of the following locations was the Quit India Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1942?
e_en: In August Kranti Maidan, the Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1942. It is also known as Gowalia Tank Maidan and located in Central Mumbai. On 8 August 1942, Mahatma Gandhi delivered the Quit India speech decreeing that the British must quit India immediately or else there would be mass agitations. He called for resolute yet passive resistance which meant the certainty that Gandhi foresaw the revolution, best represented by his call to do or die.

e_en: ​Pongal festival is celebrated for four days in Tamil Nadu. The fourth day of Pongal is called Kaanum Pongal. It is celebrated by south Indians during the Hindu Harvest festival. This is dedicated to the Hindu sun god, the Surya, and it corresponds to Makar Sankranti, the festival of harvests celebrated in India under many regional names. The first day of Pongal is called Bhogi Pongal. The second day of Pongal is called Surya Pongal.
